info.title: Terrain Viewer tile service
info.description:
## Quick start

Copy an address into QGIS (XYZ Tiles), MapLibre, CesiumJS or Blender. `{z}/{x}/{y}` stay as they are: the client fills them.

**Slope, Mapterhorn, XYZ tiles** (any mode of `/processes`, several comma-separated)

```
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?terrainSource=mapterhorn&modes=slope
```

**Sky-view factor, IGN RGE ALTI (France), XYZ tiles** (zoom 12 and finer; the first tiles of an area take a second or two)

```
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?terrainSource=custom-fr-ign-rgealti-highres&modes=svf
```

**Cesium terrain (quantized mesh), Mapterhorn: the layer.json** (CesiumJS, Blender's OGC 3D Tiles add-on as a *Quantized-mesh terrain* entry; delatin mesher)

```
http://localhost:3400/quantized-mesh/mapterhorn/layer.json
```

**The same, meshed by martini** (about three times faster to make, twice the triangles)

```
http://localhost:3400/quantized-mesh/mapterhorn/layer.json?mesher=martini
```

**A picture of a box** (west,south,east,north; `.tif` with one mode for its values)

```
http://localhost:3400/bbox/7.6,45.95,7.7,46/800x600.png?terrainSource=mapterhorn&modes=hillshade,contours
```

**The STAC Item of a tile** (any raster export's address plus `.stac.json`)

```
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/12/2133/1449.png.stac.json?terrainSource=mapterhorn&modes=slope
```

**The modes, as OGC API - Processes** (each mode's settings: `/processes/{id}`)

```
http://localhost:3400/processes
```

## About

What Terrain Viewer draws, as map tiles and as pictures of a viewport. Two engines draw them. The direct engine computes every 2D terrain mode in the server with the app's own code, reading the elevation with the app's own readers (tile pyramids, COG, VRT, WMS and WCS, LERC, quantized mesh, PMTiles, differences), in a fraction of a second. For everything else the app itself renders them in a headless browser, so every source it reads and every mode it computes comes out as in the app: a tile is drawn with the 2048 px block around it and the block is kept a week, so the first tile of a block takes seconds and its neighbours milliseconds. Web Mercator only.

The elevation modes are at `/terrain-tiles`, the imagery at `/basemap-tiles`. Each mode is described as an OGC API - Processes process at `/processes/{id}`: its settings with their types, ranges and defaults.

**How several modes stack.** `modes=a,b,c` draws them in one tile, in the map's order, never in the order written: bottom to top, `colorRelief`, `slope`, `aspect`, `tri`, `curvature`, `tpi`, `lrm`, `roughness`, `shapeIndex`, `blobness`, `eigenRatio`, `orientation`, `svf`, `openness`, `localDominance`, `hillshade`, `matcap`, `phong`, `shadows`, `buildingShadows`, `isoline`, `graticules`, `moundDetector`, `planeSlicer`, `contours`. The last is on top (the contours over everything, the colour relief at the bottom). `/processes/{id}` gives each mode's place as `x-tv-stack-rank` (0 at the bottom).

**Opacity.** A mode's opacity is its own parameter (`slopeOpacity`, `svfOpacity`, `phongOpacity`, ... named in `x-tv-opacity-key`) times its panel group's (`terrainAnalysisOpacity`, `reliefVisualizationOpacity`, `lightingEffectsOpacity`, listed in `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`), each 0 to 1: `slopeOpacity=0.5&terrainAnalysisOpacity=0.4` draws the slope at 0.2. The group's opacity scales every mode of the group, each one separately (not the group flattened first).

**Blending.** Over the map's background (white, black with `theme=dark`, transparent with `background=none`), each layer is drawn source-over with that opacity. The shading layers are different: the hillshade is a half-transparent dark and light layer drawn over what is under it; Phong and matcap multiply the colours under them and add their highlight; the terrain and building shadows darken. In a GIS, stack them with a multiply blend (the QGIS project does). The overlays (contours, iso-line, graticule, mound markers, plane slicer) are lines and areas over everything.

**Defaults.** Without `modes`, the hillshade alone. Given without `hillshade`, the hillshade is off. A mode's group switch does not bring the group's default mode with it (asking for `aspect` does not also draw `slope`).

**Refused together.** `basemap` with a terrain mode on `/terrain-tiles` (400: ask `/basemap-tiles` for the imagery and stack the two in the client; `/render` draws them in one picture). Any terrain mode on `/basemap-tiles` (400). On `.pbf`/`.mvt`, any mode that is only a picture: only `contours`, `isoline`, `moundDetector`, `graticules` and `planeSlicer` are vector (400). On `.tif` and `encoding=`, more than one mode, or a mode without values (400). `engine=direct` with a mode or source only the browser draws (400). Otherwise any set of modes stacks.

tags.name: OGC API - Processes
tags.description: The modes as OGC API - Processes processes (OGC 18-062r2), with OGC API Common's landing page and conformance. `/processes` lists every mode with its settings; a process is run by asking for its tiles: its description links them.

tags.name: Terrain tiles
tags.description: `/terrain-tiles`: the elevation modes as XYZ raster tiles, the overlays as vector tiles, a TileJSON and a QGIS project of them.

tags.name: Quantized mesh
tags.description: `/quantized-mesh`: any direct source as Cesium terrain (quantized-mesh-1.0) for CesiumJS, Cesium for Unreal or Unity and Blender. Give the client the layer.json; it asks for the tiles.

tags.name: Catalogs
tags.description: What can be named by id: sources, colour ramps, modes, and what a share link switches on.

tags.name: Viewport
tags.description: A picture of a viewport or a box, like a WMS GetMap.

tags.name: Values
tags.description: A mode's numbers before the colour ramp, in natural units: Float32 GeoTIFF for analysis (GDAL, QGIS, rasterio, numpy), or packed in a PNG for a web map.

get.summary: A mode's values as a Float32 GeoTIFF tile
get.description: One band of 32-bit floats, EPSG:3857, georeferenced, NaN where there is no data: the values the app colours, before its ramp, in natural units (the unit in the `x-tv-value-unit` header and in `/processes/{id}`). 256 px; `{y}@2x` or `tilesize=512` for 512. The same tile as a PNG for a web map: `.png?modes=slope&encoding=terrarium` (or `terrainrgb`), the values multiplied by `valueScale` (default 1) and packed as an elevation, so MapLibre's raster-dem or a few lines of numpy read them back; `valueScale` keeps small values (curvature) above the packing's step (Terrarium 1/256, Terrain-RGB 0.1). Computed by the direct engine only. Browsers do not display TIFF: Scalar's test request answers "Preview unavailable" and offers the file to download. **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

parameters.name: tilesize
parameters.description: The side of the tile in pixels.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: With `.png` in place of `.tif`: the values packed in a PNG as an elevation would be.

parameters.name: valueScale
parameters.description: With `encoding`: the factor the values are multiplied by before packing.

parameters.name: compression
parameters.description: Deflate with the floating-point predictor (GDAL's PREDICTOR=3), lossless: about a quarter of the size for elevation, half for slope, two thirds for curvature or svf, for 2 to 6 ms a tile. `none` for a reader without deflate.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source: an id from `/sources`, a tile address or a JSON configuration.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: One mode. `elevation` is the source's elevation in metres; the units of the others are listed in `/processes/{id}` (`x-tv-values`) and in the docs: slope and aspect in degrees, TRI, TPI, roughness and LRM in metres, svf and the eigenvalue ratio a share 0..1, openness and local dominance in degrees, curvature per metre.

parameters.name: appParams
parameters.description: The mode's own URL parameters of the app (curvatureMode, lrmRadius, svfRadius, opennessMode, ...). Its ramp, range and opacity do not change the values.

parameters.name: mapboxKey
parameters.description: Your Mapbox access token, for the `mapbox` source.

parameters.description: Your MapTiler key, for the `maptiler` source.

parameters.description: Your Cesium ion token, for the `cesium` source.

get.summary: A mode's values over an area, as a Float32 GeoTIFF
get.description: Like a WCS GetCoverage: the values over a bounding box (exactly: `width` pixels across it, the height that keeps the pixels square in Web Mercator, at most 4096 a side) or around a centre (`lat`, `lng`, MapLibre `zoom`, `width`, `height`). `/bbox/{w},{s},{e},{n}/{width}x{height}.tif` is the same with a box. `.png` with `encoding` packs them as for the tiles. Browsers do not display TIFF: Scalar's test request answers "Preview unavailable" and offers the file to download. **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

get.summary: A mode's values as one GDAL raster
get.description: A GDAL WMS description (TMS minidriver) of the mode's Float32 GeoTIFF tiles: one Float32 raster of the whole world, down to the source's deepest zoom, with overviews. GDAL opens its address as is: `gdalinfo "http://localhost:3400/gdal.xml?modes=slope"`, `gdal_translate -projwin ... <address> out.tif`, `rasterio.open(address)`, and QGIS (Layer > Add Raster Layer, the address as the source). The QGIS project (`/qgis.qgz`) has one such layer per mode, in its Values group.

get.summary: One XYZ tile of the elevation modes
get.description: A 256 px Web Mercator tile of the modes computed from the elevation (every mode but `basemap`), stacked as described under `modes`. For 512 px write `{y}@2x` in the address or add `tilesize=512`. The camera is the tile's: `lat`, `lng`, `zoom`, `pitch` and `bearing` are not read. The imagery is at `/basemap-tiles`. titiler's `url` (the source) and `algorithm` (one mode) are read; its address `/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/...` was removed on 2026-11-25 (404). **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

parameters.description: The side of the tile in pixels.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source: an id from `/sources`, the address of Terrarium tiles, of a COG (`.tif`) or of a VRT (`.vrt`), or a configuration as JSON with the fields of a library entry, `{"url": ..., "type": "terrarium" | "terrainrgb" | "cog" | "vrt" | "wms-raw" | "lerc" | "quantized-mesh" | "tilejson", "maxzoom": ...}`. Unset: Mapterhorn. `url` is read as the same parameter.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Who draws. `direct`: computed in the server from elevation tiles, in a fraction of a second, for the modes and parameters `/algorithms` lists as direct on a source `/sources` lists as direct. `browser`: the app in a headless browser, every source and mode, seconds. `auto` (the default) takes direct when it can. The answer's `x-tv-engine` header says which drew it, `x-tv-engine-why` why not direct.

get.summary: One XYZ tile of the imagery
get.description: The basemap as the app draws it: dated imagery (`imagerySource`, `imageryDate`), an XYZ or COG address (`imageryUrl`), or the app's named basemap and its overlays (`basemapSource`, `overlayBasemapIds` and the other basemap parameters of the app, at the top level of the query). Drawn by the browser engine. A terrain mode in `modes` is refused: ask `/terrain-tiles` and stack the two. `{y}@2x` or `tilesize=512` for 512 px. **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

get.summary: The STAC Item of an export
get.description: Any raster export's address plus `.stac.json`, with the same query: `/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png|jpg|tif.stac.json`, `/basemap-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg.stac.json`, `/render.png|tif.stac.json`, `/bbox/{w},{s},{e},{n}/{width}x{height}.tif.stac.json`. A STAC 1.1.0 Item with the Processing extension (v1.2.0): `bbox` and `geometry` of the export, `datetime` and `processing:datetime` the time of the answer, `processing:lineage` (a sentence: the source, the modes, their parameters), `processing:software` (`terrain-viewer tile-server` and its version), `processing:level` (`L3` for a map derived from the elevation), `processing:expression` (`format: x-tv-process`, the process ids and their inputs as executed), links `derived_from` the terrain source (its `/sources/{id}` entry and its tile template, or its address) or the imagery, `related` to each `/processes/{id}`, and the export as asset `data`. Computed from the address: nothing is drawn, and the caller's API keys are left out.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: `none`: no white (or black) map background, a transparent PNG to stack layers in a GIS. Direct engine only; the browser's tiles keep the map's background.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description:
The modes to draw, comma-separated (`style: form, explode: false`). `algorithm` is read as the same parameter. Each mode is a process: `/processes/{id}` lists its settings.

**How several modes stack.** `modes=a,b,c` draws them in one tile, in the map's order, never in the order written: bottom to top, `colorRelief`, `slope`, `aspect`, `tri`, `curvature`, `tpi`, `lrm`, `roughness`, `shapeIndex`, `blobness`, `eigenRatio`, `orientation`, `svf`, `openness`, `localDominance`, `hillshade`, `matcap`, `phong`, `shadows`, `buildingShadows`, `isoline`, `graticules`, `moundDetector`, `planeSlicer`, `contours`. The last is on top (the contours over everything, the colour relief at the bottom). `/processes/{id}` gives each mode's place as `x-tv-stack-rank` (0 at the bottom).

**Opacity.** A mode's opacity is its own parameter (`slopeOpacity`, `svfOpacity`, `phongOpacity`, ... named in `x-tv-opacity-key`) times its panel group's (`terrainAnalysisOpacity`, `reliefVisualizationOpacity`, `lightingEffectsOpacity`, listed in `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`), each 0 to 1: `slopeOpacity=0.5&terrainAnalysisOpacity=0.4` draws the slope at 0.2. The group's opacity scales every mode of the group, each one separately (not the group flattened first).

**Blending.** Over the map's background (white, black with `theme=dark`, transparent with `background=none`), each layer is drawn source-over with that opacity. The shading layers are different: the hillshade is a half-transparent dark and light layer drawn over what is under it; Phong and matcap multiply the colours under them and add their highlight; the terrain and building shadows darken. In a GIS, stack them with a multiply blend (the QGIS project does). The overlays (contours, iso-line, graticule, mound markers, plane slicer) are lines and areas over everything.

**Defaults.** Without `modes`, the hillshade alone. Given without `hillshade`, the hillshade is off. A mode's group switch does not bring the group's default mode with it (asking for `aspect` does not also draw `slope`).

**Refused together.** `basemap` with a terrain mode on `/terrain-tiles` (400: ask `/basemap-tiles` for the imagery and stack the two in the client; `/render` draws them in one picture). Any terrain mode on `/basemap-tiles` (400). On `.pbf`/`.mvt`, any mode that is only a picture: only `contours`, `isoline`, `moundDetector`, `graticules` and `planeSlicer` are vector (400). On `.tif` and `encoding=`, more than one mode, or a mode without values (400). `engine=direct` with a mode or source only the browser draws (400). Otherwise any set of modes stacks.

get.summary: A source as Cesium terrain: its layer.json
get.description: The layer.json a Cesium terrain client reads first (CesiumJS `CesiumTerrainProvider.fromUrl`, Cesium for Unreal or Unity, Blender add-ons that read Cesium terrain): TileJSON 2.1.0, `format: quantized-mesh-1.0`, `scheme: tms`, `projection: EPSG:4326` (two tiles at level 0), `available` level by level (whole at level 0, the source's bounds below), down to the level as fine as the source (its deepest 256 px Web Mercator zoom, less one), `extensions: [octvertexnormals]` and the source's attribution. The tile template keeps the query given. Any source the direct engine reads (`/sources`, engine `direct`): Terrarium and Terrain-RGB pyramids, COG, VRT, WMS, LERC, PMTiles, with the same API keys as `/terrain-tiles`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: An id from `/sources`, or `custom` with the source in `terrainSource` (an address or a JSON configuration).

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: With `custom`: the source's address or configuration, as for `/terrain-tiles`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The mesh's vertical error, as a share of Cesium's geometric error of the level (77 km at level 0, halved each level: 4.7 m at level 14, times 0.5 is 2.35 m). Smaller for a finer mesh (more triangles), larger for a lighter one.

parameters.name: mesher
parameters.description: `delatin` (the default): Delaunay refinement, about 45% fewer triangles and bytes than martini for the same error, 20 to 55 ms a tile. `martini`: a right-triangulated irregular network on the 257 x 257 grid, 5 to 15 ms a tile, about twice the triangles.

parameters.name: maxTriangles
parameters.description: delatin only: the most triangles a tile gets. The mesh stops refining there, worst points first, even above `error`. The default only bounds noisy or very fine sources (Mapterhorn's Alps need 7,000 to 15,000 a tile); lower it to keep a 3D scene light.

parameters.name: extensions
parameters.description: The extensions to write, for a client that sets no `Accept: application/vnd.quantized-mesh;extensions=octvertexnormals` header (CesiumJS sets it when asked for vertex normals).

get.summary: A QGIS project of a view
get.description: Every layer of the app as an XYZ layer of `/terrain-tiles` (transparent tiles, `background=none`), stacked as the map stacks them and grouped as its panel where that order allows: the overlays on top (contours, plane slicer, mound candidates, graticule, iso-line, each also as vector tiles), the lighting effects, the hillshade, relief visualization, terrain analysis, the colour relief, then the basemap (as the app draws it, with its overlays, from `/basemap-tiles`; a plain XYZ basemap as such too; Google hybrid), and a closed, unchecked group of each mode's values as a Float32 raster read by GDAL (`/gdal.xml`), for analysis. The layers the view switches on start checked, and every layer's address carries the view's settings. The query is the view, in the service's names (terrainSource, modes, imageryUrl...) or the app's own: the query of a share link works as is (terrainSourceA, show* switches, ramps, basemapSource, overlayBasemapIds...). lat, lng and zoom set the project's extent. Without a query: every layer unchecked but the Google hybrid basemap.

get.summary: The modes, as OGC API - Processes processes
get.description: One process per mode of the app (OGC API - Processes Part 1, OGC 18-062r2), top of the map first, then `basemap`. Each summary carries the `x-tv-` properties of its description (group, form, shading, stacking rank, values) and a link to it. `x-tv-groups` is the app's panel tree by process id. `?expand=true` gives every description in full (inputs and outputs), in one request; the QGIS plugin reads that.

get.summary: One mode, as a process description
get.description:
The mode's settings as `inputs`, each with a JSON Schema (`type`, `enum`, `default`, `minimum`/`maximum` for opacities) and the app's URL parameter (`x-tv-url-param`, `x-tv-type`, `x-tv-role`: setting, opacity, group-opacity or common). `outputs`: `image` (image/png, image/jpeg), `values` for a mode with values (Float32 GeoTIFF, `x-tv-unit`, `x-tv-display-range`), `vectorTile` for an overlay. What OGC has no slot for: `x-tv-group` (its panel groups), `x-tv-form`, `x-tv-shading`, `x-tv-stack-rank`, `x-tv-opacity-key`, `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`, `x-tv-switches` (the app's show* parameters), `x-tv-has-values`, `x-tv-values` (unit, description, the typical range the QGIS plugin's grey ramp starts with).

**Execution.** No jobs and no POST execution: the links with rel `http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/execute` are the mode's tile endpoints, templated (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`), with the inputs as query parameters. `POST /processes/{processId}/execution` answers 501 with those links.
